topSignals.title: FERC RM26-4 confirmed (June 18): landmark Section 206 "show cause" orders to all six US grid operators.
topSignals.text: After being flagged as imminent in this digest since June 16, FERC issued six tailored orders under Section 206 of the Federal Power Act to PJM, MISO, SPP, CAISO, ISO-NE, and NYISO. Each operator must "defend or revise" large-load interconnection tariffs within 60 days; FERC's preliminary finding is that existing tariffs are "unjust and unreasonable" for large loads (data centers, manufacturing). Focus areas: cost transparency, co-location rules, study process reform. DOE Secretary Wright formally applauded the action. SOFC read: This is not a final cost-allocation rule — RTOs have 60 days to respond and final tariff changes will take 9–12+ months. BTM SOFC deployment advantage remains fully intact during that transition; the FERC process validates on-site power as a parallel track. (FERC fact sheet; Akin Gump; DOE applauds; Power Magazine)

topSignals.title: Bloom Energy hits all-time high $329.51 (+15.4% on June 18) on FERC catalyst — now +250%+ YTD, market cap ~$92B.
topSignals.text: The FERC ruling was the dominant driver; UBS maintained Buy at $322 target, calling FERC "a clear positive for Bloom — more data centers are likely to bring their own power, and more utilities may partner with Bloom." Bernstein's cautious MP initiation at $276 (June 16) now sits 16% below market. Bloom's mid-year Data Center Power Report reinforces the 32% full off-grid target among US data centers. (TipRanks: BE ATH; Investing.com: ATH; StocksToTrade)

topSignals.title: EIA Q2 2026 Henry Hub spot confirmed ~$2.92/MMBtu — materially below FY2026 forecast.
topSignals.text: Q2 2026 average running at ~$2.92/MMBtu, below the $3.60/MMBtu FY2026 average and $3.34/MMBtu 2H26 forecast from the June 16 STEO. Muted summer demand is the driver; FY average rises with winter. LCOE flag: at $2.92/MMBtu, SOFC fuel input cost ≈ $0.028–$0.034/kWh at 55–60% LHV efficiency — among the lowest in recent years — pushing the near-term LCOE range toward the bottom of the $125–200/MWh unsubsidized band. (EIA STEO)

items.text: FERC RM26-4 outcome (June 18): See Top Signals #1. RTOs have 60 days (filings due ~mid-August 2026) to defend or revise tariffs; final tariff changes not expected before Q1 2027. Grid-connected alternatives face at least 9–12 months of continued regulatory uncertainty, preserving SOFC BTM advantage. (Latitude Media; ENR; Data Center Knowledge)

Germany EnEfG: 12 days to July 1 deadline. New DCs commissioning from July 1 must achieve PUE ≤1.2 at commissioning and ERF ≥10%; 100% renewable electricity from January 1, 2027. No new guidance or amendments issued.
Bloom Energy (NYSE:BE): Closed $329.51 on June 18, +15.4%; all-time high. Market cap ~$92B. UBS Buy $322 maintained post-FERC. BE +250%+ YTD. Bernstein MP $276 now 16% below market. (TradingKey)
Quiet day on FuelCell Energy (FCEL ~$17), Ceres Power (CWR), Elcogen, Sunfire.

lcoe.text: Henry Hub Q2 2026 ~$2.92/MMBtu (NEW granular data): Q2 spot average running below both the FY2026 avg ($3.60/MMBtu) and 2H26 avg ($3.34/MMBtu) from the June 16 STEO. At $2.92/MMBtu, SOFC fuel input ≈ $0.028–$0.034/kWh (55–60% LHV). Near-term LCOE bottom of range: ~$125/MWh unsubsidized, potentially below $118/MWh CHP-adjusted. FY average expected to rise with winter demand; use $3.34–$3.60/MMBtu for H2 and FY planning scenarios. (EIA STEO)

FERC reform timeline as LCOE factor (NEW context): RTO filings due ~mid-August 2026; final tariff changes Q1 2027 earliest. Grid-connected alternatives (PJM) continue to face $500K study deposit + $15K/MW readiness + 100% network upgrade costs until reforms finalize. SOFC BTM cost advantage quantification unchanged for at least 9–12 months. Use for project risk tables in LCOE model.
